otherApplications.what: FOMO is one tenant of Relay on this chain. relayDepository.what: Relay intent escrow. Users deposit here; allocator sweeps to solver treasury.

relayRouter.what: Relay multicall entry. Sells approve this and call transferAndMulticall.
relayRouter.orderIdInCalldata: A solver's fill is a call to this router whose calldata ends with the 32-byte order id from the deposit that paid for it on the other chain. Reading the last word is the whole cross-chain join, with no Relay API in the path. Only router calls carry it: a Transfer out of the executor inside a handleOps bundle is not a solver fill and its calldata ends with something else.

relayExecutor.what: Performs the swap and delivers tokens. Buy fills originate here.

solverTreasury.what: EOA. Fronts capital for fills; sole destination of every depository sweep.

fomoFundingEoa.what: EOA. Credits user wallets on withdrawal/refund.

allowanceHolder.what: 0x Protocol v2 AllowanceHolder. Emits no events, so a log-based listener never sees it. Outside FOMO's route: party to a token transfer in 0 of 221 FOMO bundles over blocks 57993000-57993400.

settler.what: 0x Settler, Robinhood Chain deployment. INSIDE FOMO's route: a party to the token transfers in 70 of 221 FOMO bundles over blocks 57993000-57993400, and in 8 of 11 sampled bundles it returns the proceeds to relayExecutor. No FOMO wallet calls it directly, which is why an earlier count of transactions sent from FOMO-delegated wallets (blocks 57679764-57699764) concluded it was outside the route - it is reached inside the executor's inner calls, so measure it by transfer party and not by transaction sender.
settler.emits: Almost nothing, and what it does emit is anonymous - no topic0 at all. 1 anonymous log across 45 sampled bundles, and 14 in a 500-block window on its own address. A decoder that indexes topics[0] without checking crashes on these.

fomoSells.then: in the SAME user-operation log span read the Swap logs and the RelayErc20Deposit. Scope by span, not by transaction hash - a handleOps bundle carries several users.

fomoBuyIntents.then: filter depositor by fomoWalletFingerprint, and require NO swap in the same user-operation span (a swap there means it is a sell's proceeds). Most buys landing on Robinhood Chain are paid for from Solana, so this sees a minority of them; the fill is the complete feed.

fomoBuyFills.then: filter recipient by fomoWalletFingerprint. Names the token; venue from the swap logs in the same transaction; order id from the router calldata.

gotchas: Bundles carry multiple users - scope logs per UserOperationEvent, never per receipt.
Never string-search handleOps calldata for a selector; ABI-decode and match by sender.
Four Swap event shapes carry FOMO flow: Uniswap V4, Uniswap V3, a Pancake V3 fork and Uniswap V2. Handling one silently mis-parses or drops the others. All four are in venues.swapEventShapes.
account.getNonce() reads 4337 nonce key 0 and is always 0. FOMO uses timestamp nonce keys.
callRequests(bytes32) is always false. Not a settlement check.
USDG is 6 decimals. Two 18-decimal lookalikes exist. Resolve tokens by address only.
Bundler EOAs rotate (52+ observed). Allowlisting them goes stale silently.
At least nine active AMM factories exist on this chain. A survey that finds two has sampled one user, not the chain.
FOMO trades established tokens through Relay's router and executor into established pools. New launches are a different crowd on different routers. Do not conflate them.

Uniswap V4 and V3 both carry a large share of FOMO swaps, so handle both. V4 is a singleton (0x8366a39c…) and its pools are NOT contracts - subscribe to the PoolManager address and filter by pool id. V3 is one contract per pool.
V4 PoolManager is NOT at the canonical 0x000000000004444c… address on this chain.
An acknowledged subscription is not a working one - Relay's websocket accepts a filter it never delivers on.
Solvers do not pre-position: 60/60 sampled fills swap inside the fill transaction, so nothing leaks before it.
Solana: a closed wrapped-SOL account refunds ~0.002 SOL. Ignore SOL movements under 0.005 when anything else moved, or rent gets reported as the token bought.
Solana: FOMO uses at least three routers, not one. Classify a swap by what moved; read the router afterwards.
Not every Relay depository deposit is FOMO - about 15% come from wallets carrying a different delegation. Apply the wallet code test to depositors, not only to fill recipients.
A wallet's EIP-7702 delegation is set by its first operation, so its very first buy lands before the wallet is recognisable. That one buy cannot be attributed to FOMO by any code test.

The Robinhood HTTPS endpoint is load balanced over backends with different heads. A range eth_getLogs whose end is past the answering backend's head returns fewer logs with no error. Query logs by blockHash and pin lookups to a block number, then retry when a backend refuses.
web3.py's async provider stalls under concurrency - at 25 in flight a quarter of calls hang until they time out. The listeners use raw JSON-RPC over aiohttp for anything hot.

How fast and how completely a subscription is served is a property of the endpoint and the day, not of the transport - the same endpoint and subscription have behaved very differently 24 hours apart. Do not record a figure here; measure with scripts/maintenance/compare_listeners.py when it matters.

Do not record how long anything takes, or how often it happens, where a decoder could come to depend on it. Timings and rates measured here have not held - transport delivery swung by more than an order of magnitude on one endpoint within an afternoon, and a median measured over one origin chain was read as describing every buy. Record what is true regardless of the day: addresses, topics, shapes, decimals, and the rules that follow from them. A third-party market survey may stay if it names its source and its date and nothing decodes from it; measure volume and timing yourself when it matters.

The order id joins the legs and is written on both chains: bytes 16..48 of the Solana deposit instruction, and the last 32 bytes of the solver's call to Relay's router. No third party is needed to match them.

A wallet's EIP-7702 implementation names the application behind it. FOMO is one of several on this chain, so treat the delegation as a label; filtering on FOMO's alone discards the rest of Relay's traffic.
A Relay deposit comes in two shapes and they are the same trade. RelayNativeDeposit pays in ether, has one word fewer, and is missed entirely by a listener watching only RelayErc20Deposit.

A Robinhood Chain sell settles on Solana as a solver's spl-token transfer carrying the order id in an spl-memo. FOMO's co-signer is not in that transaction, so a co-signer subscription cannot see it, and getSignaturesForAddress on the seller's wallet does not list it either - query the USDC token account.

execution.mempool: NONE. eth_newPendingTransactionFilter returns a filter id but yields zero txs. Arbitrum Nitro sequencer, no public gossip. No front-running, no mempool sniping. Edge is latency-to-sequencer plus reaction speed on confirmed state.

coSigner.what: FOMO's co-signer. Signs and pays for EVERY FOMO transaction on Solana and is account 0 of each. THE marker on this chain.

relayDepositProgram.what: Relay deposit program. DepositToken instruction = 8-byte discriminator + u64 amount + 32-byte order id. No destination.
relayDepositProgram.orderIdOffset: Instruction data is an 8-byte discriminator 0b9c60da27a3b413, a u64 amount little-endian, then the 32-byte order id at bytes 16..48. That id is what the fill on the other chain ends its calldata with.

solana.note: No code-based wallet marker exists here - FOMO wallets are ordinary Privy keypairs. Filter by the co-signer.
solana.routersNote: Registry v1 listed DFlow alone. At least three routers carry FOMO flow, with DFlow carrying most of it, so a swap must be recognised by what the wallet's own accounts gained and lost, never by one program id.
solana.plumbingNote: Present in almost every transaction. Exclude before naming the router.

rentDust.what: Closing a wrapped-SOL account refunds its rent, about 0.002 SOL, to the wallet. It appears as a positive SOL delta beside the real trade and will be picked as the bought side.
rentDust.rule: Drop SOL and wSOL movements under 0.005 whenever anything else moved in the same transaction.

settlement.what: Delivers a Robinhood Chain sell's proceeds as USDC on Solana: a plain spl-token transfer into the seller's token account carrying the 32-byte Relay order id in an spl-memo.
settlement.coSignerAbsent: FOMO's co-signer signs nothing here and appears nowhere in the transaction, so blockSubscribe or gRPC filtered on the co-signer never delivers a settlement. The sell is visible on Robinhood Chain only.
settlement.findingItAgain: getSignaturesForAddress on the seller's wallet does not return these - an spl-token transfer names the token account, not its owner. Query the USDC token account from getTokenAccountsByOwner.
settlement.observed: Over Robinhood blocks 57767865-57782865 (25 minutes), 166 deposits were settled by this address. Across 400 signatures on 15 sellers' USDC token accounts, all 120 memo-carrying deliveries came from it and no second solver appeared.
settlement.note: Relay's solver addresses rotate the way this chain's bundlers do. Re-check before relying on the address; the memo and the token-account rule hold regardless of who signs.
